Theme

School & learning

classical adjective

of ancient Greece and Rome

also classical antiquity, classical world, classical languages, classics, classical music, Greek and Latin

classical

Cic. Amic. 13: antīquōrum auctōritās (Lewis & Short)
Hor. S. 1.4.117 (Lewis & Short)

antīquus, antīqua, antīquum

declension

ancient, of the old Greeks and Romans

The Romans’ own word for what is old and venerable; the ancients, above all the ancient writers, are antīquī (Lewis & Short), and antiquity antīquitās. The classical languages are lingua Graeca et Latīna.

Other words

  • classicus, classica, classicum — classical

    declension · also used · modern · M-O s.v. classic, classical; Traupman 292

    Gellius’s word for a first-rank author (see classic, an author), used in modern Latin of the classical age (aetās classica, Egger, in Morgan–Owens) and of classical music.

  • studia antīquitātis — classics, classical studies

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. classics, classical studies

    Also antīquitātēs Graecae et Rōmānae (Morgan–Owens). A classical scholar is an antīquārius (M-O s.v. classicist), classically one fond of antiquity (Tac. Dial. 21; Suet. Aug. 86, Lewis & Short).

See also classic, classic, Latin.

SourcesLewis & Short: antiquus · Lewis & Short: antiquitas · Lewis & Short: classicus · Lewis & Short: antiquarius
